title: guest-memory-emulated-prefetch-for-paged-kv
creator: Samir Patel
description: Design and implement a guest-memory emulation layer and adaptive prefetch heuristics for the paged/blocked KV cache to reduce GPU swap events and tail latency. The emulation layer exposes a compact resident-set estimate (RSE) per model shard that approximates the working set without pinning pages; this drives conservative prefetch decisions when batch composition and token-position variance indicate impending cache pressure. Key features: (1) lightweight per-shard RSE maintained via sampled access traces and LRU-style decay, (2) a cost-model that trades prefetch overhead against expected batch latency savings, (3) a thermal/telemetry input that suppresses aggressive prefetch when GPU temperature or mem-bandwidth saturation is observed, and (4) a fast fallback path that falls back to host-staged execution for oversized requests. The goal is fewer GPU OOMs/gpu-swap stalls, reduced 99th percentile token latency, and predictable throughput under mixed-length workloads.
comments: 2025-02-19 - Samir Patel: Initial spike shows sampled RSE converges within 250ms for 90% of shards on internal workloads. Chose exponential decay factor 0.95 for access counts.

2025-02-25 - Aisha Kaur: Implemented baseline emulation and integrated a prefetch decision function into the scheduler. Bench results: 20% reduction in observed swap events on long-sequence synthetic traces; slight 2% median latency increase due to prefetch overhead.

2025-02-28 - Riley Thompson (review): Review feedback: tighten conservative thresholds for small-batch inference, add telemetry flag gating and opt-out env var for Dedicated customers, and include a tunable 'prefetch aggressiveness' in runtime config.

2025-03-03 - Aisha Kaur: Added thermal-suppression hook using device telemetry (smoothed over 1s window) and updated docs. Preparing PR to runtime-1.20 branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7128
acceptance_criteria: RSE estimation must run in <1ms per shard on hot path and produce stable estimates across 95% of samples
Prefetch decision reduces observed GPU swap events by at least 15% on mixed-length workloads representative of prod-telemetry
99th percentile token generation latency improves or remains flat in 3/3 benchmark profiles (short, mixed, long sequences)
Feature gated with a runtime config flag and opt-out for Dedicated/Private deployments; documented in runtime ops guide
Comprehensive unit and integration tests added; end-to-end perf job added to CI for regression monitoring
